diagnosis: Congestive Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF, EF 35%)

patient.key: 62M, professor, 3-week progressive dyspnea + PND + orthopnea. 30 pack-year smoking. HTN on lisinopril. Prior MI (father died of MI at 65). CXR: cardiomegaly, Kerley B lines, pleural effusion. Echo: EF 35%. This is systolic heart failure from ischemic cardiomyopathy.

ordersPlaced: Physical exam: General, Chest/Lungs, Heart, Extremities, HEENT/Neck

locationSequence.note: Kept patient in Office — should have admitted to inpatient unit

correctlyOrdered: Physical exam: General, Chest/Lungs, Heart, Extremities (edema), HEENT (JVD)
Furosemide IV (loop diuretic = first-line for volume overload)
correctlyAvoided: Stress echo / stress test — no stress test during acute CHF exacerbation

missedOrders.why: One of the FOUR PILLARS of GDMT for HFrEF. Initiate before discharge once euvolemic, not during acute decompensation. COMET trial: 17% mortality benefit. Multiple studies show predischarge initiation improves adherence. Some hospitals penalize CHF discharge without beta-blocker.

The fourth pillar of GDMT. Class I recommendation in 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guidelines. DAPA-HF and EMPEROR-Reduced: ~25% reduction in worsening HF or CV death. Can be initiated during hospitalization once past acute decompensation.
This man has ASCVD (prior MI). High-intensity statin is Class I for secondary prevention. CORONA/GISSI-HF showed no mortality benefit of statins in HF itself — the indication is his CAD, not his CHF.
Renal function and electrolytes are critical before starting spironolactone (K+, eGFR) and for diuretic safety. K+ >5.0 or eGFR <30 = do NOT start MRA.
Screening tool. Anemia worsens HF. Check before discharge medications.
Thyroid disease can precipitate arrhythmias and contribute to HF.
The most common cause of HFrEF is ischemic cardiomyopathy. A patient with known CAD and new decompensation needs troponin to rule out acute ischemia as the trigger.
Uncontrolled diabetes precipitates HF. Screen for it.
30 pack-years. Smoking causes CAD which caused his MI which caused his HFrEF. The chain starts with the cigarette.
Sodium restriction is a core HF lifestyle modification. Reduces fluid retention.
Alcohol is cardiotoxic and precipitates HF.
Dyspnea is terrifying. The patient is scared.
Indicated in CHF and smoking. PPSV23.
Age 62 — CDC recommends Shingrix at 50+. Office visit is the right moment.
Patient needs IV diuresis, monitoring, predischarge GDMT initiation, and echo. Cannot manage CHF exacerbation in the office. Location penalty: 50%.

optional.why: Will be elevated in CHF — confirmatory but not required. Does not affect grade.
Optional for accurate I/O monitoring during diuresis.
Optional — can reduce hospitalizations but no mortality benefit. Consider for rate control if AF present.

gdmtFourPillars.description: Guideline-directed medical therapy for HFrEF — all four should be started (sequentially, not simultaneously during acute decompensation)

pillars.status: MISSED — should start predischarge after diuresis
MISSED — Class I, can start inpatient

teachingPoints: Acute CHF management: diurese first (furosemide), then layer on GDMT before discharge. Never start beta-blocker during flash pulmonary edema.
The four pillars are additive — each reduces mortality independently. Missing two (BB + SGLT2i) leaves half the benefit on the table.
Location matters: CHF exacerbation with PND, orthopnea, pleural effusion = inpatient. Not an office case.
Statin is for his CAD, not his CHF. CORONA trial: statins don't help HF. But they absolutely help post-MI patients.
Pneumococcal vaccine is not optional in CHF. Smoking + heart failure = high-risk for pneumonia complications.
